title: F3 SD Card Health Check Failure Rate
dataSources: Lightroom photo exports (`lightroom:photo`), Flickr photo metadata (`flickr:photo`), ShutterCount body audits (`shuttercount:camera`), and F3 card tests (`f3:card`).
app: Adobe Lightroom exports, Flickr API metadata, ShutterCount camera audits, and F3 SD-card health checks sent to Splunk HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=f3:card
| eval status_value=lower(coalesce(test_status,"unknown"))
| eval failed=if(match(status_value,"error|fail|alert|overdue|late|stale|breach"),1,0)
| stats count as events, sum(failed) as failed_events by card_label
| eval failure_pct=round(100*failed_events/events,1)
| sort - failure_pct - failed_events
description: Measures how often F3 SD card health check records land in an unhealthy or exception state for each card label.
value: A plain failure-rate view highlights noisy devices, flaky automations, and habits that repeatedly slip.
implementation: Normalize test_status values into good or bad states and review the failure percentage per card label.
visualization: Bar chart of failure percentage by entity.
grandmaExplanation: It turns which parts of your F3 SD card health check data keep ending up in a bad state instead of working cleanly.
